To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the performance of recurrent neural networks on sequence learning tasks is highly dependent on the choice of update rule; (ii) the performance of the network can be improved significantly by evolving the weight and activation update rule end-to-end, along with the recurrent weights; and (iii) this can lead to networks with thousands(s) more units and hundreds of thousands of time steps than has been achieved by previous approaches

Evolving update rules for a recurrent neural network on the problem of character sequence memorization and prediction allows for the scaling up of the network size and the length of sequence that the network can learn to a much larger scale than has been previously achieved.
